canonical_title: Brazil announces R$2.3B sovereign AI supercomputer investment split across Chinese and US suppliers
aliases: Brazil AI supercomputer Huawei iFlytek Nvidia
treatment: Watch as a sovereign-AI infrastructure topic. Do not promote again unless supplier awards, deployed compute capacity, named models, operational availability, or material policy/supply-chain changes become concrete.
known_facts: Reuters reported that Brazil announced about R$2.3B ($444.2M) in AI ecosystem investments funded through FNDCT.
R$1.3B is intended for a Rio de Janeiro supercomputing project with Huawei and iFlytek, primarily to develop general and sector-specific large language models.

About R$1B is allocated through a tender for a separate supercomputer in Rio Grande do Norte that Brazil expects to rank among the world's top ten AI processing machines; officials expect NVIDIA to supply it.
Brazil framed the split supplier strategy as reducing dependence on any single company, technology, or country and strengthening sovereignty over data.
reinclude_only_if: The NVIDIA tender is formally awarded with hardware, capacity, or deployment details.
The Huawei/iFlytek project names or releases a Brazilian general-purpose or sector-specific LLM.
The planned supercomputers become operational or materially change schedule or funding.
Brazil announces material sovereign-cloud, semiconductor, or model-access rules tied directly to these projects.
notes: NEW watch-only topic. It is a real LLM infrastructure delta within the window, but omitted from the main adopted table to keep the brief focused on higher-signal enterprise-policy and financing changes.
